title: TEUM: Team Effect-aware Uplift Modeling for Online Games

problem.claim: In team-based multiplayer games, teammates' treatment propensity and shared treatment resources can influence an individual player's response to treatment, so individual treatment-effect modeling must account for causal team effects.

gap.claim: Existing uplift modeling methods have largely overlooked team effects arising from teammates' treatment propensity and their influence on individual responses.

contributions.claim: TEUM incorporates causal team-effect awareness into Individual Treatment Effect modeling.

TEUM combines team-effect-aware embeddings, a decoupled team-effect objective for disentangled uplift forecasting, and GAN-based knowledge distillation for flexible and efficient inference without instance-specific team information.
TEUM was deployed in the automatic incentive distribution system of a large online FPS game.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive offline experiments on two real-world online multiplayer gaming datasets and superior performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report a notable improvement after deploying TEUM in the automatic incentive distribution system of a large online FPS game.

narrative_sequence.summary: Uplift modeling estimates individual treatment effects and is used to evaluate engagement incentives in gaming.
Existing methods largely omit team effects, although teammates' treatments and shared resources can alter individual responses.
TEUM introduces causal team-effect awareness into ITE modeling through three coordinated components.
The authors report offline comparisons on two real-world gaming datasets and an online FPS deployment with a notable improvement.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical offline results.
The abstract does not quantify the reported deployment improvement.
The abstract does not describe the causal identification assumptions or treatment assignment process.
